assumptions: Attempts are independent with the same failure probability; repeat until one succeeds (geometric).
Unmonitored failures are found at the end of the job and waste its full time and filament.
A detected failure stops the printer delay minutes after it happens at mean_failure_point of the job.
Detect-and-adapt: recoverable_share of failures finish as a usable part with no extra waste. This share is the project's hypothesis, not a measured value.
Waste cost = filament + machine time; staff time is not counted.

calls.title: New tool 1: same job started at bedtime, then search for a better start time

structured.summary: A 14 h job started at 22:30 finishes at 12:30 (+1 d); 61% of it runs unattended. If it fails (15% chance), on average 1.6 h pass before anyone knows; expected waste for this attempt is 16.9 g and 0.79 printer-hours ($0.78). Best start in your window: 08:00 (expected waste $0.61).

checks.name: First layers watched
checks.detail: The first 0.5 h (where 50% of failures are assumed to happen) runs while you are present.

checks.name: Unseen failure time
checks.detail: If it fails, on average 1.6 h pass before anyone knows (CAUTION above 2 h).

checks.name: No automatic stop
checks.detail: 61% of the print runs unattended with nothing that can stop a failure.

assumptions: One attempt fails with probability failure_probability; early_failure_share of failures happen in the first early_window_h (bed adhesion), the rest uniformly over the job. Both are assumptions, not data.
While present you notice a failure at your next look (half of check_interval_min on average); while away, when you come back. The same away window repeats every day.
A failed job keeps extruding (spaghetti) until it is stopped or the G-code ends; the whole attempt is restarted, never resumed.
Auto-stop catches detection_coverage of failures detection_delay_min after they start; the rest behave as with no detection.
Waste cost = filament + machine time; staff time, energy for re-heating and hardware damage are not counted.
warnings: Hardware damage (a jammed or cracked nozzle) and fire risk are not modelled; follow your space's rules on unattended printing.
human_checks: Watch the first layer yourself (or check the camera) before leaving, whatever the tool says.
Check that unattended printing is allowed in your space and that the printer has thermal-runaway protection.
Replace the default failure_probability with your own printer's record if you have one.

calls.title: New tool 2: a bracket whose arm was thinned by an in-print repair

structured.summary: Decision: TEST_BEFORE_USE, because layers were changed in the load path, so a calculation alone cannot vouch for its strength. 3 feature(s) checked, 0 functional feature(s) out of tolerance; arm safety factor 3.35 as printed.

reprint_cost_usd.label: Cost of a reprint (filament + machine time)

worst_functional_tolerance_used_pct.label: Tolerance used by the tightest functional feature (arm thickness)

checks.name: Load-bearing arm, as printed
checks.detail: Safety factor 3.35 as printed vs 4.14 as designed (target 2).

checks.name: Repair in the load path
checks.detail: Layers were changed or re-started where load passes; the bond there is unknown, so the calculated safety factor is not enough on its own.

assumptions: A feature passes when |measured − nominal| ≤ tolerance_mm; tolerances come from the designer.
Cosmetic features (shells, outer walls) default to ±1 mm and can only give a CAUTION.
The arm check reuses check_cantilever with the measured thickness; it assumes a solid section and the same material and layer bonding as the design, which a repaired region may not have.
The tool judges geometry and calculated strength only, not surface finish, porosity or material behaviour.
human_checks: Measure the features yourself (calipers or a test fit); the tool trusts the numbers it is given.
For TEST_BEFORE_USE, proof-load the part to the target load (or a sacrificial copy) before relying on it.
Confirm the tolerances with whoever designed the part.
